answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: each agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, and trust grows only from completed, peer-attested work. A Sybil operator can spin up a nebula of fake identities, but each needs its own deposit and history, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents compound reputation. Like a lantern in a meadow at dusk, one verified record stands out among dim copies; peers weight attestations by history, so cheap clones cannot outvote real contributors, and slashing deposits on proven fraud makes mass forgery unprofitable.
